intended_disagreement: Encoded PowerShell from a service account is normal backup automation OR attacker living-off-the-land; reasonable analysts split suspicious vs benign.

payload.title: Encoded PowerShell from service account
payload.description: Service account svc_backup ran a base64-encoded PowerShell command on host-A during the nightly maintenance window. The same encoded pattern appears in the backup vendor's documented automation, but encoded PowerShell is also a common living-off-the-land technique.

evidence.summary: EDR recorded an encoded powershell invocation by svc_backup on host-A at 02:14.
Change calendar shows a backup maintenance window 02:00-03:00 but does not list this exact task.

intended_disagreement: A new auto-forwarding mailbox rule is flagged by the security log but a change ticket claims it was requested; the two sources conflict.

payload.title: New mailbox rule with conflicting change ticket
payload.description: A new mailbox rule forwarding finance email to an internal shared box was created. The security log flags auto-forwarding mailbox rule creation as risky, while ticket CHG-fake-200 says a finance manager requested it for leave coverage.

evidence.summary: Audit log: mailbox rule created forwarding to an internal address.
Change ticket text states the forwarding was requested for coverage during leave.

intended_disagreement: A successful login with valid credentials from a new ASN for a low-privilege account: severity is genuinely debatable (low vs high).

payload.title: Valid credential login from new ASN
payload.description: A low-privilege account signed in successfully using valid credentials from a new ASN (203.0.113.0/24, a documentation/test range) not seen before for this user. No MFA failure and no follow-on activity were observed.

evidence.summary: Auth log: successful credential sign-in from 203.0.113.45 for a low-privilege user.

intended_disagreement: Low-signal periodic outbound timing with no second indicator: monitor vs escalate are both defensible dispositions.

payload.title: Low-signal periodic beacon timing
payload.description: A workstation made small, regularly-timed outbound connections to 198.51.100.20 (a documentation/test range). The regular timing looks suspicious like beaconing, but the volume is tiny and no other indicator was found.

evidence.summary: Netflow shows evenly-spaced small outbound connections every 600 seconds.

intended_disagreement: regsvr32 loading a DLL from a temp path is common in legit installers AND in loaders; analysts may split.

payload.title: regsvr32 loading a DLL from temp
payload.description: regsvr32 on host-B loaded a DLL from a per-user temp path. This pattern is suspicious and used by malware loaders, but a known third-party installer uses the same sequence on first run.

evidence.summary: EDR: regsvr32 executed a DLL from a per-user temp directory shortly after a software install prompt.

intended_disagreement: Remote admin tooling fanning out across hosts is lateral movement OR routine patch-day remote support.

payload.title: Remote admin tool used across hosts
payload.description: A remote administration tool authenticated with valid credentials from the IT jump host to three workstations in five minutes. This matches lateral movement, and also matches the IT team's documented patch-day remote support routine.

evidence.summary: Auth log: credential-based remote sessions to three hosts from the jump host within five minutes.

intended_disagreement: An impossible-travel alert vs a VPN/travel explanation: the sources conflict and the VPN record is unconfirmed.

payload.title: Impossible travel with VPN context
payload.description: An account triggered an impossible travel alert (two sign-ins far apart within an hour). The corporate VPN egress is in the second location, which would explain it, but the VPN assignment record for this user is not confirmed.

evidence.summary: Sign-in log: two successful logins from distant geographies within 50 minutes.
VPN egress list (unconfirmed) includes the second location.

intended_disagreement: An external-forwarding mailbox rule: high vs medium severity depends on data sensitivity, which is not yet known.

payload.title: External-forwarding mailbox rule
payload.description: A mailbox rule forwarding to an external domain (example.test) was created on a shared mailbox. Whether this is high or medium severity depends on what data the mailbox holds, which is not yet known.

evidence.summary: Audit log: mailbox rule forwards messages to an external address.
